name: BAM-15

card.summary: A mitochondrial uncoupler that burns fat in mice and is traded online as a 'safer DNP'; no human data exist.
card.note: No human safety data; uncoupling class has documented toxicity.

quick.overview:
BAM15 is an experimental compound that makes mitochondria burn fuel as heat. In mice it cut fat mass and improved blood sugar.

Forum users discuss it as an alternative to DNP, but no human trials have been published.
quick.mechanism: It carries protons across the mitochondrial membrane, uncoupling food oxidation from ATP production and raising energy expenditure.
quick.risks: Human safety is unstudied. Uncouplers as a class can cause overheating, and DNP has been linked to fatal poisonings. BAM15 is not approved.

lead: BAM15 is an experimental mitochondrial uncoupler, a small molecule that lets protons leak across the inner mitochondrial membrane so that nutrient oxidation produces heat rather than ATP. It was identified in a 2014 screen as an uncoupler that did not depolarize the plasma membrane.[1]

People interested in leanness discuss BAM15 as a possible way to raise energy expenditure and reduce body fat, which would show up as a lower body-fat percentage and a more defined physique. The reasoning is that uncoupling burns more calories for the same food intake; in mice fed a high-fat diet, oral BAM15 reduced body fat and improved insulin sensitivity without changing food intake in studies reported in 2020.[3][4]

Online it is often compared with the older uncoupler DNP, whose history as a diet drug and whose documented overdose deaths are well recorded.[11] Wikipedia notes that the published work on BAM15 is in animals, covering obesity, sepsis, kidney injury and cancer models,[10] and no human trial results have been published.

chain: Uncouples mitochondria so fuel is released as heat
Lower fat mass at the same food intake (animal data)
angle.text: Proponents discuss BAM15 as a way to burn more energy without eating less, which they expect to translate into lower body fat and a leaner look. The body-fat reductions reported so far come from mouse studies.

paras: BAM15 is a synthetic heterocyclic compound with a fused oxadiazolopyrazine core and two fluorophenyl-amine side groups.[10] It is lipophilic and acts as a protonophore: it carries protons back across the inner mitochondrial membrane, bypassing ATP synthase.[1] The 2014 discovery paper described the screen that identified it and reported that, unlike classic uncouplers, it did not depolarize the plasma membrane, a side effect associated with the toxicity of earlier compounds in cell work.[1]
The compound is sold by chemical suppliers for laboratory use and is referred to in forum posts as a research chemical. It is not an approved drug anywhere.

Chemical uncouplers have a long record as weight-loss agents. 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP) was studied in obese patients at Stanford by Maurice Tainter, who reported an average loss of about 20 pounds in 1933; he estimated that at least 100,000 Americans used it in its first year on the market, with three reported deaths.[11] The American Medical Association's drug council declined to list it in 1935, cataract cases emerged, and the 1938 US Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act expanded FDA powers under which DNP was deemed too toxic for human consumption.[11]

DNP's mechanism was published in 1948 by Loomis and Lipmann: it uncouples mitochondrial energy production so that energy is released as heat instead of ATP, and overdose can cause hyperthermia up to 44 degrees Celsius and death.[11] Wikipedia reports that online availability raised use in the 21st century, with at least 50 overdose deaths worldwide between 2010 and 2020, that WADA banned it in 2015, and that the UK made it a regulated poison in October 2023.[11] BAM15 belongs to the same functional class, which is why its 2014 description as an uncoupler that does not depolarize the plasma membrane drew attention.[1]

Cells make most ATP by letting protons flow back through ATP synthase down a gradient built by the respiratory chain. Chemical uncouplers provide a second route for protons, so the chain works harder to keep the gradient and nutrient oxidation increases while ATP output per unit of fuel falls; the energy is released as heat.[1] The 2014 report described uncouplers as lipophilic weak acids that move protons into the matrix independently of ATP synthase.[1]

Laboratory work has used BAM15 as a tool to uncouple mitochondria in cultured cells, including studies in astrocytes and cardiomyocytes, and it has also been tested as a molluscicide on invasive snails, where it collapsed mitochondrial membrane potential.[8]
A 2020 mouse study described BAM15 as orally bioavailable, and animals in that work received it by mouth.[3] No human pharmacokinetic data have been published.

In diet-induced obese mice, BAM15 decreased fat mass, increased nutrient oxidation and improved glycemic control; the Nature Communications authors reported that this occurred without reduced food intake and described reversal of obesity-related insulin resistance.[3] A second 2020 paper in EMBO Molecular Medicine reported that BAM15 stimulated energy expenditure and glucose and lipid metabolism and protected against obesity in mice.[4]

BAM15 was reported to improve skeletal muscle quality in a mouse model of sarcopenic obesity, with effects linked to mitophagy and muscle quality control.[5] In mouse sepsis it was reported to reduce mortality and kidney injury,[6] and in an endotoxin (LPS) model it was reported to reduce inflammation.[9] Wikipedia also lists mouse studies of kidney ischemia-reperfusion injury and of cancer growth, including breast cancer and acute myeloid leukemia models.[10]

Wikipedia lists mouse and cell studies in which BAM15 suppressed breast cancer growth and proliferation (2021) and induced reactive oxygen species production as an approach to acute myeloid leukemia (2022), alongside work on kidney ischemia-reperfusion and cold-induced kidney tubule injury.[10]
No studies found. All published work on BAM15 for obesity, kidney injury, sepsis and inflammation is in cell culture or animals.[3][4][6][9]

Users on looksmaxxing and fat-loss forums discuss BAM15 as a candidate fat-loss compound and compare it with DNP, an uncoupler used in the 1930s as a diet drug and later associated with fatal overheating. Posters typically cite the 2020 mouse papers as grounds for interest and often note the absence of human data themselves. Descriptions of personal use are anecdotal; no clinical safety data exist for BAM15 in people.

Uncouplers as a class raise heat production, and the toxicity of DNP is the main reason researchers developing newer uncouplers stress safety margins. Whether BAM15 behaves differently in people has not been tested.

timeline.event: BAM15 identified as an uncoupler that does not depolarize the plasma membrane.[1]
Two mouse studies report reversal of diet-induced obesity and improved glycemic control.[3][4]
Mouse study reports improved muscle quality in sarcopenic obesity.[5]
Mouse sepsis and kidney injury study.[6]

lore.intro: On fat-loss forums BAM15 is discussed as a newer, possibly more tolerable alternative to DNP, mostly on the strength of the 2020 mouse papers.[3][4]

claims.claim: BAM15 is a "safer DNP" for burning fat
claims.believers: Proponents point to the 2014 finding that it does not depolarize the plasma membrane and to mouse studies where body fat fell without reduced food intake.[1][3]
claims.experts: The mouse studies report fat loss and improved glucose control, but no human safety or efficacy data have been published.[3][4][10]

claims.claim: It preserves muscle while cutting fat
claims.believers: Users cite a mouse sarcopenic-obesity study reporting improved muscle quality.[5]
claims.experts: That study was in mice with a specific disease model; no study has measured body composition in people taking BAM15.[5]
